subject: Re: Zephyr pilot — SLA exception request + forecast plan
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@zephyrlabs.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Timothy Sanders <timothy.sanders@zephyrlabs.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Zephyr pilot traffic estimate and short-term SLA ask

Hi Monica / Aisha —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We’re greenlighting a small pilot of Zephyr’s new in-app assistant that will hit a subset of our beta users on July 8th (two-week pilot). High level expected traffic for week 1: ~10k unique users, average session 3 requests, but we expect short bursts around product announcements.

Attached is the traffic workbook (zephyr_traffic_estimate.xlsx) with per-minute projections. The key thing we need confirmed: can Redwood support a temporary uplift to cover burst peaks up to ~120 RPS for roughly 8–12 minutes during a notification event? We’re flexible on model size and are happy to flow to a smaller model if you recommend it, but we need an explicit temporary quota/throughput guarantee so we can proceed with our notifications schedule.

Also copying Tim (procurement) — if there’s any paperwork (SLA exception, MSA addendum) we should prepare in advance, please flag it.

Appreciate quick confirmation — our internal go/no-go for announcements is EOD Wednesday.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Growth, Zephyr Labs
Samantha@zephyrlabs.com

Attachment: zephyr_traffic_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet, 14KB)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@zephyrlabs.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Zephyr pilot traffic estimate and short-term SLA ask

Samantha —

Thanks for the workbook; that helps. Quick confirmation: we can provision a controlled, time-boxed uplift for pilots, but we need a precise traffic shape and a fallback plan. Two asks from our side before I escalate for a formal SLA exception:

1) Can you fill out the per-minute peak profile on tab "EventBurst" (we need the 1-minute peak numbers, not only 5/10m aggregates).
2) Confirm payload sizes (avg tokens/request) and how tolerant you are of model downgrades or 429s during non-critical minutes.

Copying Aditya to align on capacity scheduling. If you can get the per-minute peak numbers to us by EOD tomorrow we’ll aim to lock a temporary uplift window and an operational playbook.

On paperwork — we usually do a short addendum that lists the uplift window, governance (who can trigger it), and rollback criteria. Tim, if you want a draft I can share one.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: zephyr_initial_request.pdf (request summary)
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha@zephyrlabs.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Zephyr pilot traffic estimate and short-term SLA ask

Samantha / Monica —

Reviewed the workbook. A few technical clarifications and a suggested uplift plan so the ops team can schedule it: 

- Traffic profile: if the 1-min peak approaches 120 RPS, that's roughly ~7.2k RPS-minutes over a 1-minute window. With our typical token sizes (you indicated ~350 tokens/request) this maps to ~2.5M tokens in that minute.
- Suggested temporary uplift: (a) bump concurrent request limit to 130 RPS for a 10-minute rolling window around the event; (b) provision a fallback route to a 7B quantized variant we have in catalog (reduces latency and token cost); (c) enable prefix caching for repeated prompts (if any).
- Observability: we need a small set of probes from your side (one synthetic per region) to validate end-to-end latency during the uplift.

Operational asks for Zephyr: assign a primary and secondary runbook owner who can trigger the uplift window and confirm rollback if errors exceed 5% 5xx or median latency > 900ms.

Aditya — can you confirm whether we have spare burst-on-demand capacity for July 8th morning US-west window? If not, estimate lead time to reserve.

Happy to jump on a quick call to finalize numbers.

—Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Manager, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Zephyr pilot traffic estimate and short-term SLA ask

Team —

I reviewed the ask and Aisha's recommended uplift. We can approve a controlled, one-time SLA exception for a time-boxed burst on July 8th with the following constraints: 

- Window: 10 minutes (configurable +/- 2 minutes) starting at the agreed timestamp; we will gate it behind a manual trigger from Zephyr's runbook owner.
- Limits: up to 130 RPS and a soft-fallback to the 7B quantized variant after 8 minutes if error rate or latency thresholds are hit.
- Governance: pro-forma addendum to the MSA listing uplift window, trigger owners, rollback criteria, and a cost uplift at 2x standard burst rate.
- Observability: we will create a temporary dashboard and provide a shared link; Redteam on-call will monitor for the window.

Aditya — please reserve the burst capacity and add the runbook to the operations calendar. Monica — once Zephyr gives the per-minute peak and runbook owner names, we can produce the addendum and the DocuSign link. 

I attached the internal burst_playbook.md for reference (contains trigger checklist and post-mortem template).

-Markus
Markus Klein
Director of Product, Redwood Inference

Attachment: burst_playbook.md (text, 6KB)
